searchText: If chain slows down or some validators could not propose, take some time to fix it. If block reorgs or chain crashes or hangs, pause it and fix it. Does not sound that hard. But I think all CEX and bridges will pause for a few hours watching for PoS chain to get stable and ETH prices might get volatile during that a few hours. Fun to watch Q: say a validator is supposed to propose a block, how many epochs before that time will he know that he's chosen to propose? is there a dashboard where you can see it? 2 <https://beaconcha.in/blocks> unless validator set changes or something right, then it's 1 right (the current epoch)? anything that shows 2 epochs in advance? your own node, if you want real time data the validator set is chosen every 2 epochs for the next 2 epochs afaik yes, for attestations it is. Not for proposals though <:thonk2:667665759673253899> i thought the first attestor is the proposer but im a total noob Yeah the current effective balance is used as part of selecting proposers so it theoretically is only visible for the current epoch. Though most of the time you can calculate it one epoch before and have it turn out right (but not always). can u gib some more detail on how that works? https://eth2book.info/altair/ would be my recommendation. The annotated spec will include it with commentary but the "Building Blocks" chapter also talks about randomness which is a key element. > Deliver Edition 1.0: Altair at some point before The Merge (the point at which Ethereum moves to proof of stake). By then, I aim to have done the following: <insert squinting Fry gif> Yeah, it's going to take a bit longer. Need to stop giving estimates. Adrian's reminded me to add a note about proposers not being known until the current epoch, so that's good. No worries, it's definitely an awesome resource, so keep up the good work! I mean, he's got another few days...
